notes: NIST CSWP 29 exactly as served (32 pages), cut to pages 1-14 with pypdf (see holdout/SELECTION.md): page 1 cover (artwork, title 'The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0', institute name, DOI line, date, NIST logo), pages 2-5 front matter with roman folios i-iv (Abstract, Keywords, Audience, Supplemental Content, Note to Readers; Acknowledgments; Table of Contents and List of Figures; Preface), pages 6-14 sections 1-4 (printed pages 1-9). Section 5 starts on printed page 10 (PDF page 15) and is not in the file; the table of contents on page 4 still lists it and Appendices A-C. The cover is not checked at all (it may be partly or wholly an image). Headings: the blue bold front-matter headings and the numbered section headings, as printed with their numbers. The table of contents repeats the section titles with dot leaders and page numbers; those lines are not headings, and no ordered anchor or must_contain phrase uses a section title, so a converter that writes the contents as text is not penalised. Figure captions ('Fig. 1. CSF Core structure' ...) are not headings, and text inside figures is not checked. The file has no tables (the step list and tier chart are figures), so tables is empty. must_contain: 23 phrases, each printed once in pages 1-14, none containing an em dash, quotation mark or apostrophe (the text uses typographic ones throughout) and none crossing a page break; 'which are a mechanism for describing an organization' stops before the possessive. 'Appendix A is the CSF Core' is printed twice (pages 7 and 8) and is not used. ordered: 8 body-text anchors on pages 2, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 13 and 14. Noise (visible furniture): every page after the cover carries the running header 'NIST CSWP 29' / 'February 26, 2024' / 'The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0' (13 times); 'NIST CSWP 29' is printed nowhere else (the DOI is written 'NIST.CSWP.29'), so a faithful conversion has at most 1. The date and the title are not counted because they are also legitimate cover or abstract text. The text is ragged-right; its only line-end hyphens are in compounds ('high-/level', 'one-size-fits-/all', 'sector-'), so absent is empty. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 150-300 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, mastheads, cover art, chart labels) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants, the '>=' sign), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
